title: Front brake pads and rotors
setting: Small independent shop, customer's sedan on the floor, no lift free.

steps.line: Car's on the ground, cracking the lug nuts loose on both front wheels before I lift it.
Floor jack under the front pinch weld, lifting it up. Lift's taken, so I'll just work with it on the jack, it's only a pad swap.

error.summary: Working under a car supported only by a jack
error.why: Jacks are for lifting, not holding. Hydraulic jacks can bleed down or slip, and you'll have your hands and head in the wheel well.
error.correctAction: Set jack stands at the manufacturer's support points, lower the car onto them, and chock the rear wheels.
error.consequence: The jack's seal let go while Jess was reaching behind the rotor, and the car dropped onto the rotor with Jess's arm in the wheel well.

steps.line: Wheel's off. Removing the two caliper bolts.
I'll just let the caliper hang by the brake hose while I swap the rotor.

error.summary: Let the caliper hang by its brake hose
error.why: The weight of the caliper can damage the flexible brake hose internally, which can cause a soft pedal or a pull later.
error.correctAction: Hang the caliper from the spring or strut with a hook or wire so the hose isn't stretched.
error.consequence: The hose collapsed internally, and the car came back pulling to one side under braking.

steps.line: New rotor's on. Pushing the caliper piston back with a C-clamp so the new pads fit.
Pads in, caliper back on, torquing the caliper bolts to spec. Same on the other side.
Wheels on, lugs torqued in a star pattern, car's on the ground. Keys back to the customer, they can just drive it out.

error.summary: Didn't pump the brake pedal before releasing the car
error.why: Pushing the pistons back means the first pedal press goes nearly to the floor until the pads are brought back against the rotors.
error.correctAction: Pump the pedal until it's firm, check the fluid level, and road test before handing the car back.
error.consequence: The customer backed out, pressed the brake, and the pedal went to the floor. They rolled into a parked car.

steps.line: Writing up the work order. Pads, rotors, and I'll note the rear brakes have about half their life left.
